page: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an uncommonly high memory-to-core allocation of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) alongside SHA-NI and VAES cryptography instructions. High-speed ephemeral storage is integrated via a 944 GB local NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core capabilities contrasted with limited multi-threaded throughput. Single-core stress-ng tests reach 3521.69 and Geekbench single-core reaches 2714.0, placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded compression benchmarks also achieve top-tier ratings, clocking 38.38 GB/sec in gzip and 16.86 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, due to its low total core count, aggregate multi-threaded metrics rank lower: multi-core Geekbench scores 4879.0, PassMark CPU registers in the bottom 25% at 6444.77, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to 33.01 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains solid with 402.64 GB/sec for small cached reads and 52.38 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8-2amds_v7 is tailored for workloads requiring significant RAM and low-latency NVMe scratch space without paying for unneeded CPU cores. The substantial 64.0 GB memory footprint paired with only 2 vCPUs makes it an efficient option for memory-bound applications that do not scale across large thread counts. Practical workload fits include in-memory caching layers such as Redis, memory-intensive database staging, single-threaded processing pipelines, and data manipulation tasks that leverage fast local NVMe disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is a constrained-core virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, paired with an extensive 64.0 GB of memory and a 944 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating without hardware multithreading or dedicated GPUs, the system delivers top-tier single-core CPU metrics, scoring 2714.0 in Geekbench single-core and 3521.69 in stress-ng single-core tests. While overall multi-core compute throughput is limited by its 2-core allotment, its high memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU provides strong performance for memory-intensive operations. Extended vector extensions including AVX-512 and crypto instructions are fully supported. The instance is structured for high-memory, single-threaded or low-concurrency workloads, such as memory-resident caching systems, localized data manipulation, and NVMe-backed database workloads.
